sources.verifiedBy: fetched directly from tax.nv.gov on 2026-11-10 and read: most tax-related documents and payments (returns, payments, refund claims, license applications, registrations, permits) must be submitted electronically to the Department of Taxation starting December 7, 2026 unless a waiver or exception applies; a waiver request must be submitted at least 20 days before the first applicable document is due and may be granted for up to one year (no waiver for payments of $10,000 or more, NRS 353.1467); paper is allowed while a timely waiver request is pending and during a portal technical failure of more than four hours in a day.

efile.text: Each employing unit and employer that is subject to chapter 612 of NRS shall file by electronic means all quarterly contribution and wage reports. The Division may grant a waiver of not more than 1 year if the employer lacks the facilities to file by electronic means, filing electronically would impose a severe economic hardship, or other good cause is shown (NAC 612.035).

returns.name: Employer's quarterly contribution and wage report
contents: Contributions are due and must be paid on or before the last day of the calendar month next following the close of the quarter (NAC 612.260), so April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31; filed electronically (NAC 612.035).

The taxable wage limit is 66 2/3% of the preceding year's average annual wage, rounded to the nearest hundred dollars (NRS 612.545): $43,700 for 2026 per the U.S. Department of Labor's compilation; wages above it are still reported.
The code text read does not state a weekend or holiday rule, so the next business day is assumed.

notModelled: Nevada has no state income tax on wages, so there is no state withholding.

From 2026-12-07 the Department of Taxation (not the Employment Security Division) requires its returns, payments and registrations to be submitted electronically unless a waiver or exception applies (S4). This reaches the Modified Business Tax, which is a payroll-based tax the engine documents but does not calculate; it does not change the Employment Security Division's own e-filing rule (NAC 612.035) above. A waiver request is due at least 20 days before the first covered document is due, and payments of $10,000 or more cannot be waived.
